_comment: Dataset barriers. ARCHITECTURE.md is the prose; this file is the part a
machine checks. layer_audit.py reads it and enforces two rules: one
writing process per file, and no module writing across a layer boundary
Layer membership follows what a file is a record OF, except that anything
derived, regenerable and never hand-edited is Layer E regardless of which
layer it summarizes. That one convention is what makes the crossing rule
enforceable: without it every audit and every model would legitimately
touch three layers and the rule would mean nothing.

A.name: Facilities
A.subject: Existing and operating data centers.
A.key: facility_id (planned); today the snapshots have no stable key

B.name: Proposed projects
B.subject: Announced, proposed and under-construction projects, and their lifecycles.

C.name: Opposition events
C.subject: Recorded opposition events and the entities that produce them. Joins to Layer B only through the existing entity linkage.
C.key: opp_id, linked to project_id through data/project_links.csv

D.name: Policy instruments
D.subject: Enacted and pending restrictions, the county frame they attach to, and the reference geography that frame is built on.

E.name: Derived analytics
E.subject: Everything computed from the layers above: baselines, models, audits, worklists, reports. Declared derived, never hand-edited, always regenerable from its inputs.
E.key: inherits the key of whatever it was derived from

exempt_multi_writer.master_opposition.csv: The source of record for Layer C, and the one file with more than one writer by design. scripts/build_master_csv.py refreshes it from upstream under the ownership rule that ended the 2026 corruption; census_gap_candidates.py and promote_signal_candidates.py append gated promotions only. All three are append-or-refresh under a stated ownership discipline, none of them rewrites another's rows, and every promotion lands in an audit trail. This exemption is the reason the rule exists elsewhere: it is the exception that had to be argued for.
exempt_multi_writer.data/signal_candidates.csv: A handoff, not shared ownership. signal_harvest.py writes the queue; promote_signal_candidates.py consumes it and rewrites what remains, so the file holds exactly the rows the gate did not promote. The two never write concurrently: the promoter runs after the harvester in the same workflow.

declared_crossings.signal_harvest.py: Layers A and C. One GDELT call returns both facility-lifecycle articles and opposition coverage, and splitting the network call in two would double the quota cost to separate what a single classifier can route. The module routes, it never merges: a row lands in exactly one layer's file, with the opposition side winning any tie, and neither file is a source of record.
declared_crossings.census_gap_candidates.py: Layers C and D. This is the gap-closure promotion path: a Layer D census gap becomes a Layer C opposition record. The crossing is the point of the module and it is gated (complete, dated, sourced, dedup-guarded, census-corroborated), appends only, and writes every promote, hold and block decision to data/gap_promotion_report.csv.
